paragraph: Carlstadt is a small market and the numbers reflect that. Detached single-family activity is sparse, with three sales over six months at a median of $640,000, a sale-to-list ratio slightly under asking, and a median of 32 days on market. Nothing sold above list. With a sample that small, and a range from $625,000 to $738,000, the median is the number to anchor on. Two-families are the real volume here, ten sales at a median of $770,000, and nine of the ten were two-family properties with a typical layout of four or five bedrooms across three full baths. That tier is competitive: 60 percent sold above asking, the sale-to-list ratio came in at 1.047, and the median was 25 days on market. Expect competition on the good ones. Prices ran from $640,000 to $1,425,000, so read individual comps carefully rather than the average. The monthly series is too thin to call a trend in either tier. If you're weighing the two, the deciding factor is whether you want the space and yard of a single-family or the rental income and tenant management that comes with a two-family.
